name: 922 Production Packets
description: Builds the tube cutting list a batch feeds into the 1D cutting optimizer
author: Anthony Sieben

setup: The batch's PO H<batch> Pallet & Rod Organizer must be filled out - the pallets and source materials come straight off it.
The order folders need their shop prints. Lengths are read off the assembly drawing where a tube belongs to one, and off the tube's own sheet where it doesn't.
Nothing else. The app only reads; it writes one workbook and one report.
how_it_works: It reads every tube on the batch off the Pallet Organizer and groups them by source material, split across pallets 1, 2, 3 and SAW.
For each tube it finds the saw cut length: a 'SAW CUT' note or a dimension in parentheses is taken as printed, otherwise the assembly dimension plus 0.1 for each end that gets ground.
Where two tubes on one assembly are nearly the same length it still fills both in, in length order, and marks them for you to check.
output: <batch> Tubes.xlsx in the batch's Production Packets folder - one sheet per source material, named after it, with the part name, its saw cut length and the quantity. No headers, ready to paste into the optimizer.
The sheets come out in the Material Use Tracker's order for that batch - pallet 1, then 2, then 3, then SAW - so you can read the two side by side.
Any row it wants you to check is highlighted yellow.
A Production Packets report PDF beside it, listing what needs a look, what had no drawing, which tubes have no print of their own to bind, and the full cutting list.

A TechDeck Packets folder of bound drawings: one per saw cut material with the order number stamped on and the cut length highlighted, one per laser material, one of the drawings worth checking, and one holding every other drawing in the batch.

fields.label: 922 Root (optional)
fields.description: Leave blank to find the 922 QTDR Production Packages folder automatically.
